title: Chapter 213: Boss Chen
html:
“Boss Chen, tell me the truth. What is happening to my brother? Will he relapse?” The more evasive Chen Ge became, the more anxious Wang Hailong felt.

“I don’t think it can recur, because it was never an illness.” Chen Ge tried to reassure him. “Don’t dwell on it. What matters now is helping Shenglong return to an ordinary life.”

Wang Hailong tried to respond, but Chen Ge continued. “Your brother has been isolated for years and has grown accustomed to shutting himself away. That will make recovery harder. If possible, bring him outside more often.”

Chen Ge pitied Wang Shenglong. An innocent boy had been reduced to hiding in a van’s darkest corner for fear his appearance would frighten strangers.

“I discussed it with our father, but how can we take Shenglong out like this? If people point and stare, won’t that make everything worse?” Wang Hailong shared the concern. The thin monster was gone, but its trauma would take years to heal.

“Didn’t I introduce you to a psychologist? He may be able to help.” Looking at Wang Shenglong hiding silently in the corner weighed on Chen Ge as well. “Reconnecting with the world will take time. If you need anything from me, ask.”

As he turned away, a tentative idea occurred to him. He looks frightening but has a gentle heart. If nowhere else will accept him, perhaps he could work at the Haunted House. Xu Wan is too petite to look like a murderer. Wang Shenglong’s size better matches what visitors expect.

When he returned, the shelter was one-third complete and the benches were already arranged. Rather than visit other attractions, many guests sat and waited for their turn at the Haunted House.

“Xiao Chen, your Haunted House has become remarkably popular.” Uncle Xu sounded impressed. “I overheard several visitors say they traveled hours by train just to come here. Now that you’re famous, focus on management and give them the best possible experience. Impress them, and every visitor becomes free publicity.”

Chen Ge had reached the same conclusion. Terror was among the strongest human emotions, and almost everyone shared a frightening experience afterward. Even if a visitor summarized the entire attraction with “It’s scary,” that might be the finest praise a Haunted House could earn.

Chen Ge played the killer in Murder by Midnight while Xu Wan portrayed the bride in Minghun. Three hours later, many visitors had survived both scenarios. Some had endured enough; others rested before challenging Mu Yang High School.

To prevent accidents, Chen Ge followed each group through Mu Yang High School from a distance, dressed as Doctor Skull-cracker. By noon, the best performance belonged to six visitors who found fourteen name tags in twenty-five minutes.

Many visitors fled as soon as they realized how different Mu Yang High School was. The underground exit remained unlocked, allowing anyone to leave at will—but anyone who regretted quitting had to join the queue again.

Is finding twenty name tags too difficult?Chen Ge considered it. Everything he did was meant to improve the visitor experience. The mannequins feed on fear and screams, so they’re becoming more lifelike. At this rate, no one will reach the Third Sick Hall this week.

After some thought, he lowered the requirement to sixteen name tags. No one succeeded. “These visitors are too timid. I almost miss those medical students.”

Chen Ge pulled the gates shut and helped Xu Wan remove her make-up.

“You may miss them, but I doubt they miss you.” Uncle Xu counted tickets outside. “Business has gone well these past few days. Keep it that way. Don’t make anyone faint or vomit again. You’ll frighten me more than the visitors.”

“Don’t worry. I’ll try to keep it under control.” His phone rang before he finished. Seeing He San’s name, Chen Ge smiled. “Calling at a moment like this—could this be a sign?”

Chen Ge sat on the steps and answered. “Boss! The owner of Tian Teng Medical School wants your number. May I give it to him?”

“Wants my number?”

“Yes. After you left, chaos broke out at Tian Teng Medical School. The visitors split into two camps. One claimed Tian Teng’s reputation was undeserved and demanded refunds so they could visit your Haunted House instead. Their loyal fans argued that of course you weren’t frightened—you own a Haunted House yourself.”

“What does any of that have to do with the owner wanting my number?”

“Everything! To avoid disappointing his fans, the owner promised to visit your Haunted House and prove that one Haunted House owner won’t be frightened by another’s attraction.” He San sounded positively delighted. Chen Ge suspected some of his own wickedness had rubbed off on the student.

“They’re coming tomorrow morning with their fans. Apparently, they plan to record everything and humiliate the visitors who demanded refunds.”

Chen Ge was rather speechless. “Are these mindless fans?”

“No idea, I’m just calling to warn you.”

“Give him my number. We’re in the same business; better communication benefits us both.”

Soon after He San hung up, an unknown number called.

“Hello?”

“Boss Chen, I own Tian Teng Medical School. We met recently.”

“Yes, how can I help you?”

“We plan to visit your Haunted House tomorrow, accompanied by some fans. I hope you’ll show us mercy.”

“Of course. You know I don’t hold grudges. My Haunted House welcomes all of you.”

“You’re very gracious.” The owner hurriedly added, “We’ll choose an intermediate scenario—not too frightening, but not too easy.”
